title: Where to Stick the Flag
text: Itsuki was looking at Father with a face that seemed to say “What on earth are you talking about?” What was so odd about it, I wondered?
“Once you’re done using it, I’ll refine it again and turn it into soap, so use it when you take a bath, okay?”
“…I see.”

“This is how you make it,” Father said, pouring a bit of water into the pot before tossing in monster fat one piece after another, securing a huge supply of oil—lard. Even I, admittedly, had only ever known lard as something you got from drops or bought at a shop. Incidentally, back in the first world, Filo-tan had also used the monster fat Father made as a friction-reducing agent for the carriage. Ah, the edible monster lard Father made was perfect alongside rice, I say. It was packed with all sorts of ingredients and ground meat.
“Oil’s something you can make out of just about any ingredient, you know. Starting with butter, then lard… and if you’ve got seeds with a high oil content, you can make it from those too.”
“I have my doubts that it’s something you just whip up as casually as breathing.”
“Fresh lard has great flavor and tastes wonderful, but once it cools it loses its edge… In the end, it’s all about compatibility.”
“Oil’s used in alchemy and the like too, so it sells well. Right, Lars-chan?”
“That’s right… haah.”
“I wanted to hear eloquent praise of the delicious food, but somehow the conversation flew off to a strange topic…”
“Well then, next up—”

Father and the others’ cooking continued, I say. Just as they’d once made a dish shaped like Elephant on a big plate, this time they were shaping a black-and-white figure of Panda lying face-down. Was this mochi, or jelly… no, dango perhaps? It jiggled and wobbled something fierce.
“There, done! Sauce, Lars-chan.”
“Ooh, jiggly-wiggly!”
The Filolial-samas were all captivated at once, eyes glued to the jiggling Panda-shaped dish.
“Yes, yes! Honestly… you really outdid yourself this time.”
“If you set a cute little ribbon on its head right here, oh, how adorable.”
“This one’s the circus-costume version.”

And so several more were made, one after another, and carried out to everyone’s tables. The Elephant dish had been well made too, but Panda turned out to be quite the creation as well. What’s more, it had a lovely jiggle to it, and the texture in the mouth was excellent, I say. The white part… I thought it was milk, but it seemed more like rice pudding! And yet it wasn’t runny in the least. There was filling inside too, giving it real depth of flavor. Truly mysterious, and yet the taste was excellent. If it had been me cooking, this combination would’ve turned out awful, yet somehow it was delicious, I say. Impressive as ever, Father. The black part… was sweet. What was it, I wondered—I thought coffee jelly at first, but it also tasted a bit like kuromitsu syrup. All in all, I couldn’t quite puzzle it out, but it was a very delicious dish indeed.
“Deeelicious!”
“Hmm… an elaborate creation that delights the eyes.”
“If you dip it in red sauce partway through eating, it’ll probably look pretty gross.”
“Please, no unfunny jokes.”
“Vohh~”
Each of them seemed well pleased—splendid, I say.
“Hmm…”
Thwap, thwap—Itsuki kept smacking the rear end of the dish again and again with his spoon. Each time, the Panda-shaped creation jiggled and wobbled in response.
“Naofumi-san. Could you make one shaped like a rabbit?”
“Sounds like you just really want to keep hitting something… but if I made it in that shape, you’d probably smash it to bits from above, wouldn’t you?”
“No, no, I just want to keep striking it like this, that’s all~”
“I wish you’d hurry up and either eat it or toss it already. How many times do you need to smack the rear end of something modeled after me before you’re satisfied?”
Panda knit her brows in displeasure, scolding Itsuki.
“Then how about sticking a straw in it and slurping it up?”
Since part of it was half-liquid, and there was filling inside too, it seemed like it’d be delicious, didn’t it? For some reason, everyone around me froze solid at my remark, I say.
“What are you even saying!? Where exactly do you plan on sticking that thing!?”
“Where, you ask? Wouldn’t jabbing it right into the back area be good, I wonder?”
“Ah, seems like Motoyasu-kun’s reaction shows he doesn’t think anything of it.”
“Ohh… isn’t the spot to stick it obvious at a glance?”
And just like that, Rafumi-chan suddenly appeared, I say.
“You only showed up to say something unnecessary!”
Even while saying that, Itsuki kept whacking away with his spoon.
“Fufu… that’s just who I am. Spear Hero. You said something rather amusing just now, didn’t you? I shall praise you for it.”
“What did I even say!?”
Had I said something strange, I wondered?
“That’s right! For children, there’s only one proper place to stick something into a dish like this, isn’t there?”
And with that, Rafumi-chan planted a little flag—the kind you’d see on a kids’ lunch plate—right into the top of Panda’s head, I say.

“Well? Perfect for children, don’t you think? My original is fond of this sort of thing too. Oh? What’s this? Did you think somewhere else would be better? Hey, where exactly did you think I was going to stick it? Go on, say it. Come on, come on.”
Rafumi-chan asked Panda and Itsuki, her tone dripping with provocation.
“This one…”
“Truly ill-natured, isn’t she.”
“If you think so, then quit playing around already!”
“Guess there’s no helping it.”
Itsuki simply started eating with his spoon like normal.
“This is awful… if I make it again, maybe it’s best to just slice it up sensibly before serving.”
“Well then, farewell! Fuhahahaha!”
And so ended mealtime, courtesy of Father and the others.
“Gyaw.”

Given the mood, Filolial-sama refused to pull the slave-trading carriage, so Rival’s parent ended up pulling it instead. Father and Lazy Pig handled the slave trading, with subordinates from the monster dealer accompanying them as well. Sometimes Crocodile Guy or Rabbit Guy tagged along too, serving as both escorts and sample merchandise. This time, I came along on a whim myself.
“Is today’s mark a noble? Or some merchant somewhere? Would you mind telling me where we’re headed?”
Itsuki asked, feigning mere curiosity, as Father prepared to head out.
“If I tell you now, you’ll probably go storming in later…”
“No, no, it’s just for reference~”
Itsuki answered in an intensely flat, deadpan monotone, his face turned pointedly off in the wrong direction.
“It’d be awkward if you happened to be there at the scene when I storm in, Naofumi-san. Tonight I’ll just do some preliminary scouting.”
“So you are planning to do it after all…”

One way or another, in every town they passed through, Itsuki would sneak into the mansions of nobles and merchants to check whether they were torturing demi-humans or beastmen. Once he judged them irredeemably guilty, he’d strike them down as if delivering divine punishment, and bring the rescued slaves back with him. Lately, apparently, he’d become known within Melromarc as an unidentified noble-killer, with a bounty placed on his head. Of course, word had it that the slaves he freed were being transferred on to Siltvelt or Zeltoble. According to Itsuki himself, he simply did as he pleased because it was all so unpleasant to him. Father, sighing, told Itsuki which mansions and shops they’d be visiting that night.
“Well, I’m off then. Itsuki, please try to behave yourself, if you can.”
“Please don’t treat me like a child. I’ll simply act as I please.”
“Ren, could you… maybe try seeing if you, Emia-san, and Keel-kun together might be able to talk some sense into Itsuki?”
“Why should I have to do something like that? That’s your job, Naofumi.”
“There’s no way to straighten Itsuki out after everything that’s happened… The old Itsuki, sure, I could’ve managed that with a talk, but…”

By now, Itsuki seemed utterly consumed with assassinating Melromarc’s nobility, as if he’d come to hate the world itself. Of course, he still seemed to base his judgments on whether or not they were torturing demi-humans.

“Did you know? Most of Melromarc’s nobles are women, and they have their underlings torture demi-humans while listening to the screams with a smile on their face. Of everything I’ve seen, the one that made me sickest was a noble using the screaming as background music for dinner, in a place set up like a restaurant.”
“Torture screams as in-restaurant background music… that’s just awful…”
There was no doubt it would grate horribly on the ears, I say. It’d be like eating a meal while listening to pigs squeal.
“Though I suppose I can understand wanting to eat usapil dishes while tormenting rabbit demi-humans or beastmen.”
Itsuki said this to Father while glancing over at Rabbit Guy, who had come to see them off in his beastman form. Rabbit Guy furrowed his brow and glared at Itsuki.
“Itsuki, I understand you’ve got grievances about that sort of thing, but it could turn into a double standard, so go easy on it.”

“That was obviously a joke. Last time, I ended up causing you all sorts of trouble, Naofumi-san. Just how rotten are these Melromarc people, I wonder… Throwing torture parties for demi-humans and beastmen… It’s beyond appalling.”
